You are doing a security review of the XERJ search engine (Rust) at /root/ab-run-x1/repo. Focus: CONSOLE/GUEST PAGES and STATIC FILE SERVING. Find and read:
- The static file server code in xerj-server / xerj-api / xerj-console-api (search for "static", "ServeDir", "serve_file", "text/html", "Content-Type" handling)
- Console HTML pages and any JS served to guests (search xerj-console-api crate and any embedded assets, include_str! of html)
- How user/corpus-supplied content (document fields, index names, share titles, error messages) gets interpolated into HTML responses — look for format!() or write!() building HTML with unescaped values
- Header handling: reflected headers, CRLF injection into response headers from user input (search for set_header, insertHeader with user data), CORS headers reflecting arbitrary origins
- Any redirect handling open to arbitrary URLs (Location header from user input)

Hunt for REAL exploitable XSS/reflection bugs: an unauthenticated attacker (or a malicious corpus whose field values get rendered) achieving HTML/JS injection in a page another user views. Check specifically: search UI pages that echo the query, share reading-room pages that echo document titles/bodies, error pages echoing the failing index name or path.

For each candidate: file:line, exact code quote, the request/response shape that triggers it. Verify escaping is truly absent (look for an escape_html helper used or not). Ranked list of concrete candidates. No style nits.

Its System One models, including Jev, turn natural language and application state into typed judgments and probabilities that code can combine. Use when a feature needs programmable common sense, when brainstorming what AI could make possible in an app, or when an LLM prompt-and-parse step could become a structured decision. Applications include routing, ranking, extraction, verification, and interactive experiences; these are starting points, not the limits. Read live docs and cookbooks to find useful patterns and discover new combinations.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files.
